description: Figure 5(a) is a line plot that illustrates the training loss curves for different methods during training from scratch. The x-axis, labeled "#Iteration," is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 140,000, with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis, labeled "Loss," is a linear scale ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays six distinct lines, each representing a different method: Vanilla (purple, solid line), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue, solid line), SepLLM (n=64) (orange, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green, solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red, solid line), and SepLLM (n=128) (dark blue, solid line). All methods start with a high loss value, approximately 3.3, and exhibit a rapid decrease in loss during the initial iterations. The loss curves for all methods converge to a similar low value, around 2.6, after approximately 100,000 iterations. The SepLLM (n=128) method shows the fastest initial decrease in loss, followed by SepLLM (n=64, H/T), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64), StrmLLM (n=64), and Vanilla, which has the slowest initial decrease.
